Sublemma: replace variable object spaces by discrete object sets before localizing at fully faithful essentially surjective functors (Gepner–Haugseng Theorem 5.3.17).

title: Discrete-object reduction for localization of enriched categorical algebras
statement:
Let $\mathcal V$ be a monoidal infinity-category, with nested universes large enough for all the categories below. Use the categorical algebras (also called algebroids), enriched functors and fully faithful essentially surjective functors of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Explicitly, an algebra with object space $X$ has mapping objects $A(x,y)$ and coherently associative unital compositions, encoded by a functor $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ preserving coCartesian arrows over inert maps; $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}$ is classified by $[n]\mapsto X^{n+1}$. Its underlying infinity-category has mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(\mathbf1,A(x,y))$. Fully faithful means equivalences on mapping objects; essentially surjective means every target object is equivalent in the underlying category to an image object. Write $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathcal V)$ for these categorical algebras with variable object spaces, and $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathcal V)_{\mathrm{Set}}$ for its full subcategory on discrete object spaces. Let $\mathrm{FFES}$ denote the fully faithful essentially surjective functors in either category. The inclusion induces an equivalence of homotopy coherent localizations
$$\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathcal V)_{\mathrm{Set}}[\mathrm{FFES}^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathcal V)[\mathrm{FFES}^{-1}]_\infty.$$
This is an equivalence of infinity-categories, including their mapping spaces and coherent compositions, natural in monoidal functors of the enriching category.

source.place: Gepner–Haugseng, Enriched infinity-categories via nonsymmetric infinity-operads, Theorem 5.3.17 (sets versus spaces) and its functorial inclusion; Definitions 2.4.5 and 4.1.1. Read online; archive WANTED. Older numbering 5.2.17 in the proof of Haugseng rectification Theorem 5.8. No Stacks tag supplies this enriched discrete-object reduction. Completion itself is the existing lem-coef-algebroid-completion, not a new assertion here.

proof.text: Put $E=\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$ and let $p:E\to\mathcal S$ be its object-space projection. By [lem-coef-algebroid-object-space-fibration] this is a Cartesian fibration for the arbitrary monoidal $\mathcal V$ in the item. Apply the first comparison of [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-localization-comparison] to the terminal ordinary category $D=\{*\}$ and the empty set of localization arrows. Evaluation at $*$ identifies its simplicial presheaves with $\mathrm{sSet}$, its objectwise weak equivalences with weak homotopy equivalences, and $\operatorname{Fun}(N(D)^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ with $\mathcal S$. Thus objectwise passage to spaces gives a localization $j:N(\mathrm{sSet})\to\mathcal S$, with the full functor-category universal property. Form $E_\Delta=N(\mathrm{sSet})\times_{\mathcal S}E$, with projection $j':E_\Delta\to E$. An object is a simplicial model $K$ together with an algebroid whose object space is identified with $jK$. Pulling back further along constant simplicial sets $c:\mathrm{Set}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ gives $E_{\mathrm{Set}}$, the subcategory in the item: the realization of $cI$ is the disjoint union of one point per element of $I$, naturally in $I$, so $j(cI)$ is the discrete space $I$. On $E_\Delta$ define $W_\Delta=(j')^{-1}(\mathrm{FFES})$; on $E_{\mathrm{Set}}$ this is the stated class $\mathrm{FFES}$. These are the enriched functors of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. The equivalence-class description of essential surjectivity used here agrees with the surjectivity of $\pi_0\iota$ in the current [def-coef-complete-algebroid], by the object-equivalence criterion of [lem-coef-algebroid-object-space-fibration]. All categories are small after the permitted universe enlargement.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.17 proof, first two pullback squares

proof.text: Construct the right adjoint $s$ to $i':E_{\mathrm{Set}}\to E_\Delta$. The constant-simplicial-set functor has right adjoint $K\mapsto K_0$: a simplicial map $cI\to K$ is exactly a function $I\to K_0$, since every higher simplex of $cI$ is the unique degeneracy of a vertex. For $(K,A)$ define $s(K,A)=u_K^*A$, where $u_K:j(cK_0)\to jK$ is induced by the vertex map $cK_0\to K$. By the Cartesian mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-algebroid-object-space-fibration], maps from $i'B$, for $B$ with object set $I$, to $(K,A)$ are the disjoint union over simplicial maps $cI\to K$ of the fibrewise spaces of algebra maps $B\to f^*A$. The corresponding disjoint union for maps $B\to s(K,A)$ is identical under $\operatorname{Hom}(cI,K)=\operatorname{Hom}(I,K_0)$. This natural identification of mapping spaces, induced by composition with the restriction map $\epsilon_{K,A}$ below, shows that $B\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{E_\Delta}(i'B,(K,A))$ is represented by $s(K,A)$ for every $(K,A)$; by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion] the representing objects assemble to a right adjoint, so this constructs $i'\dashv s$, with identity unit $si'\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and counit $\epsilon_{K,A}:i's(K,A)\to(K,A)$ the restriction map over $cK_0\to K$.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.17 proof, construction of the right adjoint s

proof.text: The counit is fully faithful by the restriction formula of [lem-coef-algebroid-object-space-fibration]. Every component of $jK$ contains a vertex of $K$: a point of the geometric realization lies in the image of some simplex, and the straight segment inside that simplex joins it to the image of a vertex. Since $j$ is passage to the homotopy type, the same component assertion holds in $jK$. Paths in the object space give equivalences in $A$ by the fibration statement, so every object of $A$ is equivalent to an image of a vertex; the counit is essentially surjective. The functor $i'$ preserves FFES, since its underlying enriched functor is unchanged. So does $s$: full faithfulness is the same mapping-object equivalence restricted to vertices. For essential surjectivity, start with a target vertex, choose an equivalent image object under the original functor, and replace its source object by a vertex in its component. This gives an equivalence between the required target and a source vertex image. It is an equivalence already in the restricted algebra: its arrow, inverse and inverse identities use exactly the same mapping spaces and composition as in the original algebra. Hence $s(W_\Delta)\subseteq\mathrm{FFES}$.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.17 proof, FFES counit and preservation under s; direct verification in place of invoking Proposition 5.3.9

proof.text:
After localizing, $i'$ and $s$ induce functors in opposite directions because of step 3. Their unit and counit induce natural transformations by the functor-category universal property of localization: compose the original transformations with the localization functors and use the fully faithful restriction equivalences on functor categories. The unit is already an equivalence and every counit component lies in $W_\Delta$, so both localized transformations are equivalences. The localized functors are therefore inverse equivalences
$$E_{\mathrm{Set}}[\mathrm{FFES}^{-1}]_\infty\simeq E_\Delta[W_\Delta^{-1}]_\infty.$$
This is the elementary unit/counit argument of Lemma 5.3.14, written here rather than made into a new node.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.14 and first equivalence in the proof of Theorem 5.3.17

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-localization-cartesian-pullback] to the localization $j$ constructed in step 1 from [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-localization-comparison], and to the Cartesian fibration $p$ of [lem-coef-algebroid-object-space-fibration]. The weak homotopy equivalences contain all equivalences of $N(\mathrm{sSet})$, namely simplicial isomorphisms; $j$ has the full functor-category universal property; and $p$ is Cartesian. Therefore $j':E_\Delta\to E$ is localization at arrows $T$ whose base is a weak homotopy equivalence and whose image in $E$ is an equivalence. In particular $T\subseteq W_\Delta$: an equivalence of algebroids has an inverse enriched functor and hence is fully faithful and essentially surjective. Restriction along $j'$ identifies functors out of $E$ with the full subcategory of functors out of $E_\Delta$ inverting $T$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.16 and second comparison in the proof of Theorem 5.3.17

proof.text:
Under the restriction equivalence of step 5, functors inverting FFES correspond to functors inverting $W_\Delta$. The forward implication is immediate from $W_\Delta=(j')^{-1}(\mathrm{FFES})$. Conversely let $H:E\to\mathcal T$ have $Hj'$ invert $W_\Delta$, and let $F:A\to B$ be FFES in $E$. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-model-arrow-lifting] to the functor $p:E\to\mathcal S$ and to the passage-to-spaces functor $j$ of step 1. It gives an arrow $\widetilde F$ of $E_\Delta$ whose image under $j'$ is equivalent to $F$. FFES is unchanged by equivalence of arrows: inverse enriched functors induce inverse mapping-object maps and inverse equivalences on underlying objects, and the same is true after composition. Thus $\widetilde F\in W_\Delta$, so $H(F)$ is an equivalence. This identifies the full subcategories of functors inverting the two indicated classes for every $\mathcal T$, including their mapping spaces. By the homotopy coherent localization universal property it proves
$$E_\Delta[W_\Delta^{-1}]_\infty\simeq E[\mathrm{FFES}^{-1}]_\infty.$$
Composing with step 4 yields the equivalence induced by the original inclusion.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.17 proof, last localization comparison and composition; model-arrow representation isolated in the cited supporting node.

proof.text: For a monoidal functor $\mathcal V\to\mathcal W$, postcomposition on algebras commutes with restriction in the object-space fibration and preserves FFES by [lem-coef-algebroid-object-space-fibration]. It therefore gives a commutative square of the original inclusions and, by localization's functor-category universal property, of their localized functors. The horizontal functors are the equivalences just proved; their coherent naturality is inherited from postcomposition and the fully faithful restriction on functor categories. All localizations and equivalences used are those of infinity-categories. Consequently mapping spaces and coherent compositions, not just homotopy-category Hom sets, are retained.
